swp.name: Ship/Weapon Pack
swp.author: DarkRevenant
swp.description: Adds high-quality ships and weapons that fill missing roles in Starsector. This mod is meant to look and feel like vanilla Starsector, enhancing your experience with the game. This mod also includes the International Bounty Board (IBB), a series of difficult boss-fight bounty missions featuring unique ships to face off against.

descriptions.text1:
The Ko Combine r4501 "Herdmaster" was to push the standard for high-end civilian drone tenders with unmatched reliability, low cost, and internal volume given to crew comfort. An attempt at further pushing frontier-work with a larger hull that was up-armoured for combat and supercharge factory-spec systems for greater burst speed and weapon function. But the pre-collapse world was not as dangerous or barren as to necessitate the increases in self-defense or self-sustain. As such it was forgotten, the prototype left to rust in some long lost junkyard. Or so it was before an entrepreneurial lad had come upon it.

Soon after coming into possession of his 13th ship, the captain came upon a great fortune, a derelict Herdmaster-class - class yet unseen but briming with potential in the post-collapse hellhole and even an intact production chip for the hull, an amazing haul for any. However while entering the derilict for salvage Joeson had an encounter, a great and eldritch entity proclaimed to him to become a paragon of humanity he must chose one over thirteen. Joeson being a man of great charisma and and slight delusions of grandure, took fully to such a grand task, deciding on scrapping his lucky ships he ordered his grandiose assembly to begin on the spot, him and his men working night and day to repair the Herdmaster with the hulls and systems of all 13. The result of this was a ship to shepherd humanity to a new golden age. However expending all of their supplies for the masterwork, they were forced to head straight to the nearest port, scraping off excess parts of the ship, the crew willingly sacrificing themselves in a fight against unknown foes from deep space to keep the dream alive.
Or at least that is what was claimed by Joeson, as he returned ragged and alone atop what was his magnum opus. Even in its "imperfect form" the Herdmaster was enough to inspire the impovrished and opressed miners and unfortunate and forgotten salvagers to take up arms and rise, led by their new master - Joeson.

The Ko Combine r450 "Shepherd" sets the standard for civilian drone tenders with unmatched reliability, low cost, and internal volume given to crew comfort. A wildly popular combat modification package has been assembled by various survivalist and pirate groups, the mk.III consists of specifications to up-armour the hull for combat and supercharge factory-spec systems for greater burst speed and weapon function. Even modified, and re-modified the Shepherd mk.III is fragile, so similar how it was in civilian life it relies on a drone to do its work, a "Borer mk.VI" improvised combat drone.

The "Borer mk.VI" is built on six hardy, maneuverable semi-autonomous "Borer" drone chassis welded and SuperDuctTM taped together, retaing their shielding suitable for hazardous operations in which high radiation or physical impacts may be expected. No longer used primarely in mining, salvage, nor cleanup applications, they have been enhanced for combat aplications. The mk.VI mod gives the crude AI the capability to control six mining beams at the same time..

The demise of the Joesonites was not in vain, their modified and recovered hulls have made their way onto the wider Sector market. Through the generous hands of their slayers.

Quite possibly the first test run for a twin active system loadout, this Wolf-class has been refit with a ballistic hardpoint, thicker armor, thicker munitions and more crew saftey features, however these additions came at the cost of losing it's shields. Not to be outdone by the constrained space within the ship, the Scrapyard's engineers simply bolted on a flare system to defend it against missiles, nothing much else would be hitting it in combat, thanks to the superior range of ballistic weaponry.

The usual privateer trick of stripping cargo holds and replacing them with fighter bays, weapon mounts and armor is as old as spacefaring and still kicking, because it works, and it still works here with the Warmule-class.

A homonculus crafted out of a Mule and a Venture, the Warmule can be outfitted to succeed in any field of combat thanks to it's generous and diverse amount of firepower.

An Eagle-refit-based strike cruiser. The Whitetail features an impressive engine and autoloader combo capable of easily decimating most ships if piloted well. A grand leap for Doyle engineers utilizing modern ablating composites and subsystems to achieve an antique doctrine.
A hardy Conquest-based blueprint mod built for deep ventures into the outer reaches of the Sector, able to be outfitted for any threat thanks to it's various weapon mounts and fighter bays.

Discarded Monitors are hard to come by, but whenever one appears the Ashbird Scrapyards is one of the first players to aim at entering it into their ranks. The highly damaged frames which are acquired this way require heavy refitting and repair, in the process often losing some combat capability and changing enough from their original hull to be reborn as a new classification of ship.

A simple escort that just barely scratches the size required to be considered a small destroyer, it features an inbuilt powerful PD weapon that continuously denies a large area and defensive systems for saving the ship if it gets caught out of position.

The ship has been heavily modified by the Ashbird Scrapyards at a blueprint level and no original blueprints remain. As should have been their right, being the ones who techmined it, however the Hegemony argued that as a corporation part of it, the Scrapyards were under an obligation to check in any high value finds before proceeding, this lead to a protracted legal battle resulting in the Scrapyards moving on as an independent corporation and losing all of their Hegemony-provided planetside assets.

The Ashbird itself, a highly modified version of the already unusual Uguns-class. Arkan personally oversaw merging it with an earlier scrap-rig flagship and a [                     ] found by him in [                                                               ], which serves as both a [                 ] and symbol of might.

A series of semi-ill-advised modifications have been made to militarize this normally-harmless hull. Whether it's more dangerous to its crew or its enemies remains a point of contention at dockside bars, but these modification are often favored by pirates seeking to create the impression of overwhelming firepower.

The Hermes is a small, dependable cargo hauler often converted for transport duty among poor frontier worlds. Its crew and passenger facilities are charitably described as "robust" but it manages to get the job done with remarkable consistency despite the primitive maintenance facilities it frequents.

Factory-spec, the Hermes is armed only for "active collision avoidance", but its turret system is often upgraded to achieve nearly full albeit light point-defense coverage that can destroy the stray missile while escaping from active combat zones. This firepower is meagre compared to dedicated combat ships so only a mad or truly desperate captain would employ the Hermes in front line combat.

A series of semi-ill-advised modifications have been made to militarize this normally-harmless hull. Whether it's more dangerous to its crew or its enemies remains a point of contention at dockside bars, but these modification are often favored by pirates seeking to create the impression of overwhelming firepower.

One of the smallest ships in the Sector equipped with an on-board hyperdrive actuator, this class is typically used for safely transporting VIPs or couriers between star systems.

Although small, the Shuttle-class is outfitted for the comfort and security of its potential VIP passengers. It is rare to see one in combat; if a captain is unlucky enough to be in such a spot, one can quickly see why: most power systems on board are reserved for use by the life support, comfort and entertainment modules, installed to make sure that passengers do not get bored on long voyages.

The Atlas-class superfreighter is a prime target of pirate attacks. A few are later found at the broken heart of a sharp spray of impact debris in some lonely orbit. Others earn a pirate's second appraising glance and are hauled off to secret shipyards. Cargo holds are fitted with munition storage racks and struts holding up missile hardpoints.

This Atlas, reborn in vaccuum and fire, now delivers a cargo of death from the hand of a pirate warlord.

A crude but deadly Dominator refit. One of the earlier Scrapyard designs and one of their pirate exports, it is not particularly pleasant to look at but if it gets its "hands" to range up with the enemy it can certainly "clap". To aid in its aggressive endeavours it mounts an advanced blast drive system which utilizes a variable release exotic shaped charge to boost speed while pursuing or strafing. 

Marketing to pirates is suprisingly easy, a visible one hundred per-cent increase in gun will sell to most small timer even if the sacrifices under the hood make the craft dubious.

Originally funded and pushed through regulators as a way to "get miners more invested in their work", the Homage is a homage to mech fantasies of aeons past. It features in-built reinforcements and more "mining" power than most ships of a similar size, making it very appealing to aspiring "space knights" and mercenary keepers of order.

Based off a Cerberus-class freighter, this ship has been retooled to have a very capable set of frontal mining tool slots, with a bridge moved further back and centered to provide better accuracy during manouvers in asteroid dense locales.
A Digmaster-class vessel with its weapons systems linked and overdriven to the maximum allowing for truly incredible 'mining' potential.

A small and angry sister ship of the Vigilance, the Gryphlet-class lacks the staying power of its bigger sibling, however thanks to the lighter profile and advanced targeting system it performs far better in a strike role.

The pinnacle of Doyle Futures Antiques engineering intended to safeguard their corporate worlds for eternities to come, each Tyr-class ship is outfitted with a Neutronium hypercube core providing functionally infinite feedstock to its grand array of autoforges and repair bots. Additionally the ship is armed with a classification-pending level autopilot AI allowing limited function to remain even when all crew have passed. This approach to defence unfortunately has numerous downsides which lead to the few ships created being irreplaceable pieces of art.

This unassuming Falcon-Gryphon halfbreed hatchling isn't gifted in survivability, however it holds a large missile slot and a dual system setup giving it the capability to output a great amount of burst damage and keep the damage going for a respectable time.

A great success in combat that suggests the best alternative to a shield or phase cloak is the capability to output enough fire to nullify any defensive advantage the enemy may have. This emboldened and funded Doyle Futures Antiques for future shieldless ventures.

The Cropthrough-class is a cute little ball of armor and a sizeable fighter bay capable of launching faster and stronger fighters than usual, paired with a recall system the ship can output a steady stream of rapid and hard to shoot down bombing runs.
An Eagle-class cruiser that has been refit for a more tactical approach to combat...

The Fleek-class is an Eagle based cruiser performing a role more akin to a scaled up Hammerhead. A good amount of weaponry with great turret arcs can be fitted on the armored ship, together with it's refire rate boosting ability, a Fleek-class is a deadly force on the battlefield able to rapidly disable anything that crosses it's path. Similar to many other high firepower and sustainability ships, many pilots like to turn off all safety features to allow them to truly push the craft to its limits.

Durable, reliable and cheap, three words you would normally never use to describe to a phase vessel but the Brightshell is. Taking the overdesign option from the 'overdesign or pray' choice faced by ring cloak ship designs it features a smooth phase journey and damper to fall back on. Weapons are a little limited for the weight class.

The aptly named Supercrusher is a simple ship packing a whole lotta heat and armor, an array of ballistics and missiles backed up by ammo feeder overdrives and missile rack accelerators make quick work of any enemy, but work quick you must as the ship lacks any shield generator and will rapidly succumb to prolonged warfare.

The Distraught-class is a capable fleet anchor with exceptional armor, respectable mobility and great weapons coverage all blostered by a unique subsystem which improves functionality under prolonged flux grid stress.

The Lil Pal-class is a light combat support craft armed with an ammoforge, auxiliary loading assist microdrones and not much else. Capable of greatly boosting nearby allies ballistic warfare capabilities as long as it is kept safe in the back lines.

Some historians believe such craft were commonplace back before the advent of built-in ammoforges coming standard with ballistic weaponry, as hard as it may be to believe that there were ever times so barbaric.

Harmless in a fair fight but terribly rude and disruptive in a fleet standoff, the Slur-class frigate is armed with one of the most advanced electronic, psychologic, informational and ideological warfare suites known to the Sector. Capable of causing disruption and confusion in enemies of flesh and blood and steel and circuit alike.

Be it lack of imaginative engineers or eccentric investors willing to take a grand flight of fancy, most 'mech' type ships are stuck around the fighter to destroyer size. Additionally pieces of advanced field manipulation technology are usually not intended for dual-purpose use as crude melee weapons. The Undertaker-class battleship breaks both of these stereotypes by being a classic low-tech array of guns riding atop a huge hypertunnel clasp with two extendable grav-phase anomaly generators that can in conjunction grab, hold and throw another craft of almost any size. An incredibly powerful tool in coordinated fleet battles.

One of those 'techmined' blueprints that just seem like an excuse for someone with a blueprint printer to glue together as many mounts as the chip will hold. This one features two weapon arrays set up to recalibrate between forwards focused and flank focused fire, unfortunately the flux grid cannot be swapped between the two at a whim and has a lengthy re-recalibration period post-swap.

For all its quirks and the complex EMP system utilizing magnetic catalyst casing missiles to project a storm of arcing energy all over the battlefield, Stormfront-class is often viewed as a budget Omen. This opinion is not averted by being a 3rd party import for smaller players in the Sector, ones that could not get a 'proper' support frigate.

A Brawler-class frigate which has been retrofit to be fully controllable via neural direct-link, including all repair and maintenance features which have been replaced by neural-linked repair microdrones. The space saved has been used to further modify the ship with improved jets, autoloaders, and a total disregard for safety. To aid with the immense stresses of handling this body of steel, the pilot is interred within a stasis-sleep casket which can extend their vitality effectively infinitely. These sophisticated modifications suggest external involvement in it's development and a particularly radical sect of the Path in it's use.

A ship which appears to be a pile of of modifications atop modifications, atop temporary solutions. What little of the original hull remains underneath seems to have been built to be fully controllable via neural direct-link, including all repair and maintenance features which have been replaced by neural-linked repair microdrones. The space saved has been used to further modify the ship with improved jets, autoloaders, and a total disregard for safety. It is unknown who would be willing to supply zealots of the Path with such advanced technology, and who would be capable of convincing them to use it with such reverence that they keep it long after its expiration date.
The zenith of technology as we know it.

Standard hunter-killer multi-role frigate model remolded through necessity and spite into a grownship nurtured in hidden chambers. Lacking point defense capability.

Grownships were a brief spark in spacecraft development. Invented and nearly perfected during a period of just less than a hundred cycles before the widespread adoption of the Forges, which proved to be more reliable and economical than the large biofactories needed to grow spaceworthy craft.

A grownship adapted to carrying a large armament and not much more. Sluggish when not in active avoidance stance it is not particularly popular as a permanent vessel.

Grownships are a wide classification, just as wide as otherwise manufactured ships, very few are fully biological and even fewer are alive. The model most widely employed by the Ashbird armada is mostly organic with an inorganic crew and command center which the ship is grown onto, the bio-to-bio two body effect and symbiotic link allowing a lone captain to pilot a craft to its full potential. The leathery insides of the ship only need to be patrolled for after combat maintenance.

The workhorse of the Ashbird grownship programme Liesma-class destroyers were among the first to emerge from the modified biofactories in defense of the Ashbird's Nest. Fairly standard multipurpose destroyer with a good frontal armament and defense capabilities.

Even with a new home for their biofactory operations, large portions of the Ashbird armada are still made up of second rate aftermarket hulls. The process of growing an entire ship is not as expensive as forging it, but it is a lot slower and with a far higher rate of failure.

Broad-shouldered beefcake grownship capable of withstanding and outputting punishment at near cruiser levels, while still maintaining respectable active mobility through instinctual evasion. 

The organic hull of Ashbird grownships is notable for the large nerve grid covering the entire ship and linking back to the pilot, effectively granting one of the most accurate and tactile damage reporting systems. To prevent feeling ghost pains from their ship-body while disembarked, pilots are recommended a therapist and psychoanalyst, very few follow these recommendations.

The very first beast dreamed up by the madman who sought out the resurrection of grownships. The Uguns-class is a capital in size, armament and battlefield presence with an agility rivalling a fighter in bursts and above average while its afterburners cool down.

It is a testament to the resilience of growntech that even when handled with post-Collapse technology a behemoth body such as this comes out of the vats with mostly minor, usually benign, overgrowths.

An ancient example of advanced phase technology, once capable of sowing panic and mayhem across whole fleets as it invisibly slid between ranks while deploying electronic and disinformational disruption. In the modern sector it still performs admirably, even lacking modernized phase coils and other crew comfort advances.

Dug up from the same techmining operation as the Nightlord and Profanity classes the Oomer-class was the hardest sell as its strange build and armament clearly display its age and experimental nature.

A phase cruiser actually capable of standing its ground and fighting other ships on equal footing, the Nightlord comes armed with an improvised coil discharge feature allowing it to turn the constant turmoil p-field turmoil surrounding it into a powerful defensive tool.

Intended to tour frontier systems the class was built capable of housing many thousands and self sustaining human habitation for prolonged periods. The Archliner, was an arcology ship, one of largest projects by Mbaye-Gogol and a rare sight even pre-Collapse as its immense size prevents the use of the Gate system and it has to be constructed on site in special temporary docks.

As such only a dozen or so were ever constructed in the Persean, all seen as exorbitant flights of hubris they nonetheless proved valuable humanitarian assets in the early Collapse chaos and even more valuable improvised military assets in the AI Wars and the ensuing troubles. Though of the number present before the Collapse many have since fallen victim of disrepair or gunfire. Most recent and notable have been the three sisters which responded to Daud's call and fell to defend Chicomoztoc.

A particularly rare specimen, to call the Pingviins-class ahead of the curve would be to terribly misrepresent just how off the curve its features go. Featuring both an efficient phase cloak and shield matrix its hybrid grownship-mechanical cyborg hull is stressed to the extreme every second of combat.

Most reputable Domain scientists denied the notion that organic matter or living organisms withstood p-space better than forged mechanisms, most.

A surprisingly competent retrofit of an Apogee-class Cruiser which maintains most of its non-combat functionality aside from the crew quarters which, along with the main gunnery module, have been replaced with autoloaders and reinforcements for a ballistics emplacement.

Compact but surprisingly comfortable frontiersman craft with a built in sensors array and long range laser spectrography assisted modular sensors mount, a high power throughput modular slot which has found new life in the post-Collapse world.

One of the most recent Orion Shipyards original products put to print shortly before the Collapse. The Blastcap features a heavy ballistics compliment and powerful engines, allowing it to take battlefields by storm and a hail of bullets.
[                                       ] Ko Combine [                                                                                 ] unknown origins.
[                                       ] Ko Combine [                                                                                 ] unknown origins.

A Champion-class vessel reborn in a backroom deal between an entrepreneurial pirate baron and an equally opportunistic, unknown R&D division. The far more practical frontal missile tubes have been replace by a bootleg ballistics nest which is used by the other modification, an experimental particle stabilization algorithm based on traditional ballistics and particle modulation interplay.

A high-brow exploration and frontier scouting destroyer still following most pre-Collapse safety and comfort regulations, though its remote probe forges and racks have been refit to carry munitions instead. Unfortunately its engines have not received the same aftermarket treatment, leaving them at the mercy of its emergency boost systems.

Possibly the greatest and most overlooked success the Doyle corporation had. Combining state-of-the-art material sciences with p-space space bending technology and a proprietary combat stress management system results in this fun-sized wrecking ball capable of tearing unprepared fleets to shreds by itself.

The Manhatten-class was created to serve a defensive fleet anchor role in small patrols, it achieves this passably thanks to its defensive fighter array and area denial Stinger bomb deployment tubes. An internally unpopular post-Collapse development forged during the brief and unsuccessful doctrinal shift leading up to the return of CEO Sun.

Sister ship to the Manhatten-class hull, taken to a different extreme by the Doyle Future's Antiques corporation. Uses hypermaterial ablatives and an overcharged engine system to push a full frontal assault at all times of battle.

The Doyle corporation was an anomaly in doctrine and pursuits which garnered them a small but loyal base of investors and customers, though their innovations were largely unappreciated by the Persean population and their branch was quickly subsumed by the Tri-Tachyon Megacorporation post-Collapse.

The Whitetail frame apparently impressed the Supreme Executor enough to order a set of these great birds to serve under the Lion's flag. However as with all Lion's Guard hulls, there are numerous deviations from the base design, including the loss of the ablative armor, the booster jets and secondary missile system, replaced by a standard shield array and an energy focus, which the Lion views more favourably. Advanced Doyle subsystems are observable throughout the internals which serve to better transfer the ship to the Sindrian elite's energy based doctrine.

The appearance of authentic Doyle corporation subsystems in this Lion's Guard refit would hint at certain elements of the company surviving its liquidation at the hands of CEO Sun.
It that should not exist.
A smaller ship of a similar build as the Undertaker.

A reckless hellspawn of a pirate modship, poorly maintained adapters rest in jury rigged nests constructed atop the Brawler-class frigate's once reliable ballistic infrastructure. It nevertheless is capable of similar ordinance output as its standard hull, provided its outfit satisfies its esoteric redundancies.

Depending on who is interviewed the Portley-class is described as anything between an adorable big boy and a fat pile of crap. The former reviews coming form outlaw rigger crews reliant on the makeshift craft for daily income and sustenance, while the latter come from patrol officers baffled by its incredible bulk.

A scrapheap, the Scrapheap 'class' of ship are a loosely similar set of makeshift homemade bandit hulls. Most are decorated and fitted differently, however all share similar shape and redundant, unreliable weapons logistics, suggesting a centralized base blueprint pirate "engineers" follow.

A Vigilance-class frigate, which the fanatics of the Luddic Path have made this ship their own, stripping out all unnecessary or heretical furnishing and transforming it into a haphazard vehicle of holy war.

An advanced, very efficient grownship made by the Exodyne Biotech corporation to fill a generalist strike frigate role. Individual armored scales and a dense semi-organic compound webbing which appears to serve as a fully grown shield system ensure the ship can regenerate on its own from most injuries, given enough sustenance.

Having to leverage a large portion of their resources to land a concession which allowed them to stay in business and appropriate the remnants of many smaller firms which liquidated at the time. The Exodyne corporation had very little pull in the grand scheme of Domain politics after the biotech bans.

A modern take on the age old LIDAR system, the Pinetree-class destroyer aims to be an escort partner to larger ships by pressuring select targets with its many smaller arms while maintaining a powerful rearwards defensive package.

The Ko Combine has always been one for total reliability on the frontier or pushing the boundaries of efficiency through specialization, the Crackshot-class takes to the latter approach with gusto. Intended to serve as the hammer to the somewhat renown anvil of the Monitor-class, it never quite achieved the same success as its older sister ship due to the reliance on an under represented specialist role to be present and alongside it.

"Moneymen and merchants are the blood of the Nation. Without them the resources each limb produce and need would not circulate."
-Unknown

"Scholars and teachers are the vertebrae to the Nation's spine. Though a nation may be a hydra, hard to decapitate, damage to the spine will paralyse it."
-Unknown

"Warriors are most obviously important, the claws of the Nation that fend for it. It takes exceptional hubris to not recognize the purpose for claws on a cat."
-Unknown

"The populace itself, the very body of the Nation. Most important but most often forgotten by ill fit rulers, a nation without muscle is already a corpse."
-Unknown

A poorly maintained and highly modified instance of a Profanity-class phase frigate. Its pirate crew have repurposed its coil instability into a p-tremor generator and stripped out the alt-war array, replacing it with a powerful standard arm.

An ancient example of advanced phase technology, once capable of sowing panic and mayhem across whole fleets as it invisibly slid between ranks while deploying electronic and disinformational disruption. In the modern sector it still performs admirably, even lacking modernized phase coils and other crew comfort advances.

An advanced, very efficient grownship made by the Exodyne Biotech corporation to fill a strike and linebreaker frigate role. Individual armored scales ensure the ship can regenerate on its own from most injuries, given enough sustenance. This class appears to eschew shields in favour of more efficient armor and numerous flare ports.

Due to the limits enforced on biotech, Exodyne had very few self-sufficient branch offices. Though the Persean branch did their best to accumulate power after the Collapse, they quickly fell as collateral damage in the First AI War.

An advanced frigate constructed utilizing experimental pocket folding hardpoints, while the implications of the project were promising the lack of upfront firepower obliterated any chance at widespread success in the Domain-wide market.

An Ashbird original design which far more closely resembles a normal ship. The Liikyis twists an organic hull around a mostly inorganic array of amenities and subsystems, including a large cargo hold and numerous standard frontiersmanship tools. The only unique feature is an advanced set of salvage-repair drones capable of reassembling hulks into semi-functioning semi-automatic droneships.

Numerous reports correlate that the Ashbird Research and Development wing could not create such advanced mechanical repair systems themselves, likely yet another techmined relic, yet again not shared with their Hegemony allies.
It is certainly an energy-mass signature on your sensors.

Heavily modified pattern of Mora-class cruisers recently spotted in use by outlaw forces which mounts an impressive kitchen sink approach to combat. Additionally certain reports suggest the ability for limited use as a makeshift dry dock and heavy forge provided enough raw material.

An eccentric design excelling in pursuing weaker targets or jumping between enemies to strike fast and fade between retaliation. Like many similar designs it too was techmined and subsequently banished to lay in a blueprint library until claimed by a desperate faction.

Sometimes even through the harshness of the Sector there are outlaws who abandon their past ways and seek to atone. The few of those that then join the Justicar Errant often end up on modified rigs such as this. Refitted by pirate engineers seeking redemption, their hallmark jury-rigging is still present.

A thoroughly confusing design written off by most well regarded historians as a chip printing error. Less reputable theorycrafters draw attention to its incredible shield matrix efficiency, well hidden structural weak points and its near perfected logistics profile, all signs that intelligent design put together this ship with a purpose. However such a purpose likely will remain a mystery as it is held back by a lackluster energy management grid. Modernized as far as it can be, it is barely passable, even with its incredible shield.

A boisterous custom job frame, the Jest-class is a capable disruptor and combatant beloved by the Fikenhild stars-to-be. The charitable Justicar Errant attracted many such idealistic warriors content with working for exposure.

Style almost trumps substance on this massive frame. It's arms repurposed from maintenance duty to simple accessory and the heavy sockets on its hips permanently fused into stage equipment, while technically still combat capable thanks to the broad array of armament, the engineers at fault for the existence of this craft are likely delusional.

An advanced, very efficient grownship made by the Exodyne Biotech corporation to fill a generalist strike destroyer role. Individual armored scales and a dense semi-organic compound webbing which appears to serve as a fully grown shield system ensure the ship can regenerate on its own from most injuries, given enough sustenance.

Reports claim that shortly before the Collapse the Persean Exodyne branch commissioned a Mbaye-Gogol arcology ship, the current whereabouts of which are completely unknown. Most likely lost during the First AI war along with any charter records but some legends say it fled the sector, though none can agree on whether it was on a journey to brave the Orion-Perseus Abyss back to Sol or complete abandonment of the ruins of the Domain which had shunned them.

An advanced, very efficient grownship made by the Exodyne Biotech corporation to fill a strike, linebreaker cruiser role. Though light for it's weight class it makes up for it with powerful burst focused armament and a comprehensive weight redistribution manoeuvrer assistance system - a tail.

Exodyne, while with a comparatively modest presence, still kept many of its most fun and abhorrent tools and toys around in cold storage for a day just like the Collapse. Fortunately for the Sector at large, the arrival of the XIV and their amicable stance towards the corporation kept most of the wildfire options at bay.

A highly experimental hull, produced by the KO Combine corporation soon after the Collapse. Allegedly based on schematics acquired from a recently-at-the-time liquidated masonry company which had attempted to venture into ship construction. The incredible complexity of the Stormcaster EMP array and diversity of the weapon outfit argues against it being drawn up by a first timer.

An exceptionally cheap, simple and dangerous handicraft hull mounting little in the way of crew comforts and a sizeable missile hardpoint. Making up what it lacks in staying power by providing acceptable up front survivability and firepower.

This hulk with life support mounts just enough weaponry to be a noteworthy threat on the frontline, not worth much beyond noting its existence. Though the various grey and black market docks found housed within the long forgotten hangars of abandoned mining outposts are often inspiring with how much is possible with just the leftover components that are too expensive to recycle.

A frigate hull modified by the Exodyne corporation, refitting most of its internal structure with biomechanical or biological components allowing for roughly equal performance at slightly lower maintenance costs. Additionally, the retrofit theoretically allows this hull to carry significantly more weapons than the base spec would be able to, however using all of them at once requires subjecting the internals to dangerous mixtures of stimulants which rapidly degrade their health.

It is likely that the bio-mechanical interwoven matrix was kept hidden under a thick layer of standard hull to hide it from the prying eyes of passing spacers, these ships only showing their true forms in battles where there likely would not be any witnesses to report back to the Domain about biotech misapplication.

A cruiser hull modified by the Exodyne corporation, refitting most of its internal structure with biomechanical or biological components allowing for roughly equal performance at slightly lower maintenance costs. Domain-era entries about this hull appear to have gaping holes in the description on the finer function of the biological components, likely indicating [  nothing being out of the ordinary  ] if certain conditions are met.

It is likely that Exodyne are not the only independent Domain-era actor that have barely survived the throes of fate. There are rumours of ghost ships utterly invisible to any sensor, great immortal warriors clad in ivory tending to their endless watch, and time vampires who take lives yet unlived, all hidden in the shadows of the Core or somewhere on a fringe decivilized world

This ship lacks any markings, designations, denotations, or even just loose bits of info often shared in Domain-standard intra-hull user manuals. Its luxurious crew space and certain, usually inconspicuous, features which line up with Domain Corporate safety standards indicate it is of bleeding-edge affluent corporate origin.

An awfully unusual hull that has been built to specialize in almost-humanoid melee combat at spaceship scale. Widely considered combat unviable, it nonetheless sees use by the radical Justicar Errant who enjoy the thrill and message melee combat sends.

This hull was initially recovered by the Church and the only known blueprint underwent numerous changes to sanctify its more heretical components so that its protective nature would be pure. However a change of leadership almost had it destroyed for the poorly understood effects of its quantum plasma-matrix link which it utilizes to defend nearby friendly fighters from damage, this was only barely averted by the intervention of the future head of the Justicar Errant purchasing the blueprint.
Crew leave their posts to reload missiles from internal storage, this leaves the ship completely immobile and defenseless.

Flux can not be dissipated in p-space, resulting in a constant buildup that forces the ship to come back to normal space eventually. Subjective time passes more quickly for the ship and its crew while in p-space.

The phase cloak generator is large and has significant power requirements, and so generally replaces shields as a ship's primary means of defense.
