descriptions.text3: Grants ability to gain and benefit from STYLE to nearby allies, effect persists as long as they continue to entertain.

descriptions.text1: Flames out engines with an explosive boost, launching towards a target. Additionally activates integrated dampers and shock plates nullifying impact damage and redirecting it to ricochet off ships.
descriptions.text3: Flames out engines with an explosive boost, launches towards a target. Nullifies impact damage and redirects it to ricochet off ships.

descriptions.text1: Context sensitive multipurpose system which activates additional manouvering thrusters and utilizes the mass of the tail to perform a maneuver. Either launching the ship in a direction while using the tail to swipe away threats or slithering forwards rapidly.
descriptions.text3: If activated when moving towards an already nearby target or in any other direction, launches the ship in a direction while using the tail to swipe away threats, otherwise slithers forwards rapidly.

descriptions.text1: Activates arm mounted shield reinforcement and projection matrices, damage taken by shields is greatly reduces and damage taken by nearby fighters is taken by the ship instead. Power is routed away from weapons and active flux purging is disabled for safety reasons.
descriptions.text3: Greatly reduces shield damage taken and redirects damage taken by nearby fighters to self. Weapons and venting disabled.

descriptions.text1: Activates an EMP emitter integrated with the ship's engine array, granting increased speed and agility as well as striking at nearby targets with powerful arcs.
descriptions.text3: Activates an EMP emitter integrated with the ship's engine array, granting increased speed and agility as well as striking at nearby targets with powerful arcs.

descriptions.text1: Activates some poorly understood mechanism to completely erase a volume previously-surrounding the ship. This erasure is quickly amended by mechanics understood even less.
descriptions.text3: Temporarily erases nearby volume.

descriptions.text1: Overcharges biological infrastructure present within the ship by injecting a potent mixture of stimulants and growth accelerants. Grants similar effects to Safety Overrides and allows the ship to temporarily use more weapons.
descriptions.text3: Grants similar effects to Safety Overrides and allows the ship to temporarily use more weapons. Slowly builds hard flux while active.

descriptions.text1: Overcharges a completely biological bubble difference generator by injecting a potent mixture of stimulants and growth accelerants. This novel system is capable of replicating the functions of some older patterns of phase skimming technology while being significantly cheaper. Prone to lashing out.
descriptions.text3: Briefly accelerates the ship in the direction of its movement. If a smaller enemy ship is within close range [  nothing special happens  ] .

descriptions.text1: Toggle a vast array of incomprehensible subsystems which render the ship completely invisible to most sensors. The obvious reliance on electronic warfare technology would explain away the function of the system to simply be an overgrown jammer-scrubber, which clears the ship's existence from enemy tactical data. However certain eccentricities in the system's function such as its aversion to any physical contact beyond standard vacuum-of-space microparticles might imply an applied quantum-void state being used to scrub the ship from truly being unless the location it might be is physically forced into by another object.
descriptions.text3: Turns the ship completely invisible, taking damage or being too close to enemies disrupts the effect. Effectiveness affected by ECM rating difference.

descriptions.text1:
A cockpit and part of the hull of a Shepherd-class drone tender, with all valuables and non-necessary vitals stripped out and stuffed with reaper torpedo warheads which get shot out at anything unfortunate enough to not have enough mobility to avoid the subpar jury-rigged missile AI and stripped down engines.

Capable of delivering ship-cracking explosions, while also being slightly guided. A truly dangerous weapon in the right hands, only outweighed by it's limited ammo for the size of the mount.

One can easily mount a makeshift rail assembly onto just about anywhere another weapon could go, slap a missile on it and you have a great weapon for scaring the life out of unwitting freighter captains. However the small increase in burst damage potential is likely not worth the inefficient construction and the herculean undertaking that is reloading one of these.

A single unguided torpedo of devastating yield with a powerful on-board engine.

An experimental strike weapon, the Sower torpedo is a large self-propelled, armored, unguided delivery system for a warhead dealing an impressive amount of directed kinetic force. The science behind the surprisingly compact detonator is poorly understood in the Sector though widely speculated to be based on physics classified as secret by Domain authority. What is known is that even one of these slipping through PD arcs may be enough to fully stress the shields of even the largest capital ship.
This simple but powerful weapon system consists of a launch tube and a magazine usually carrying five standard Sower-class torpedoes.

Dual launcher system capable of launching a torpedo barrage. Devastating to slow ships that can't move out of the way in time.

A very large weapon system, the Cyclone-class launcher is listed as having two large torpedo tubes with an internal magazine that carries twenty Sower torpedoes. The fire control system is linked, and fires two Sower-class torpedoes in tandem. An automatic loader prepares the next salvo from the magazine in seconds.
A nearly perfect 2 to 1 downscale of the infamous Assault Chaingun, ups and downs and all. Known to be prized by Lasher aces, and no one else�

The Conventional Rocket Accelerated Munitions gun uses the internal autoloaders of a ballistic mount to feed shell sized rockets to a flux efficient firing device, delivering high payloads while being able to calculate firing arcs over it's allies, all at the cost of a slow, PD vulnerable projectile.

This cannon utilises an exotic two stage armor piercing shaped charge shell to rip large chunks out of the typically thick spaceship armor. However these chunks tend to fly back and hit allies.

Terribly inefficient due to the self damage when used by a shielded ship. However if one was to be pursuing a shieldless doctrine investing in resurecting HESC technology would certainly align with their goals.

Cheap utility laser that is hardwired for missile and fighter defense. This configuration gives it longer range than most point defense weapons.

A Mk I mining laser features a fluoride gas gain medium refitted for combat. The micro-asteroid targeting package has been repurposed to track and target incoming missiles. Mostly useless for anything larger or armored targets. Has a built-in 670nm tracker beam.
The miner's best friend, this weapon can deliver pulverizing bolts of energy at medium range, albeit at extreme cost in flux.

A magnetic acclerator fires an inversely polarizatied, high heat fuel mixture that burns through weaker substances in seconds and sticks to shields causing them to destabilize rapidly. Terribly ineffective against armor. Generally less powerful than a regular beam PD emplacement but far more deadly against shielded fighters, additionally useful if a ship is outfitted with advanced, fragile optics that cannot survive the necessary beam turret agility for optimal PD.
The prototype flux-ion weapon that never quite was. Built off the Plasma Cannon, it shares a similar damage profile at reduced efficiency and with a reliable shield piercing EMP storm.
An upscaled Annihilator Rocket system capable of unleashing an unyielding barrage of missiles. A deep ammo pool helps it sustain the pressure for a length of time.

This marvel of engineering is a near perfect 2 to 1 upscale of the already infamous Assault Chaingun, all of the ups and downs included. Few ships are actually capable of fully utilizing the insane spew of high caliber explosive slugs produced by this weapon.
A forwards facing compressed flux shunt calibrated to not destabilize shields, deals damage and reduces flux based on flux level.
Highly capable Point Defense missiles capable of destroying or incapicating fighters and missiles. Ammo pool is rich but still limited.

Weapon mounting points are inherently connected to the flux grid and it should not be impossible to mount flux vents and capacitors into the space where a weapon system would go. And it is not, though such a modification comes with its own flaws and safety concerns that are at fault for such a practice not being widespread.
A small storage processing unit and a tightly secured box of goods fitted neatly into where a weapon should be, great for pacifists and people who forget freighters exist.
A storage processing unit and a tightly secured crate of goods fitted neatly into where a weapon should be, great for pacifists and people who forget freighters exist.
A large storage processing unit and a tightly secured container of goods fitted neatly into where a weapon should be, great for pacifists and people who forget freighters exist.

A quaint little bay for a few human-sized armor plate welder drones and steelfoam dispensers. Capable of repairing nearby armor plates at a passable rate though being modular and makeshift by nature makes it vulnerable to damage unlike any built in repair systems.

A respectable maintenance site for a squad of human-sized armor plate welder drones, steelfoam dispensers and even housing an armor patch mircroforge. Capable of repairing nearby armor plates at a respectable rate though being modular and makeshift by nature makes it vulnerable to damage unlike any built in repair systems.

A set of missile microforges rewired to produce fighter navigation and coordination microbuoys, so small that most shipbound sensors cannot detect. These along with the small flight control center increase agility of the ship's figthers.

A guided can of explosives, hopes and dreams. The canister is proximity fused to cover an area in Devastator projectiles and shred fighters and frigates alike. Some courageous captains may use these at point blank as a High Explosive shotgun rivaling even the Reaper's destructive force.

Sabot racks are notoriously hard to install and incredibly ugly, shipwrigths often need to carve out large parts of the hull adjacent to a missile hardpoint just to fit the missile trio. To solve all this and more a slow autoloader is used to store and load more missiles than a rack ever could.

Long range, rapid fire, accurate and packing a decent bit of kinetic energy, this gun stands out amongst its energy weapon peers and would overtake them all in a heartbeat if it was not for the crippling flaw, a feedback reaction in the gravitational anomally pulser that disrupts engines and drive fields, just enough to leave anything firing this weapon a sitting duck.

A single unguided torpedo that sacrifices the devastating yield of its similarly sized ilk for what amounts to a miniature nanoforge capable of rapidly constructing hull patches and repair drones from scraps created by the blast.

An exotic design to say the least and as with many of the other exotics, Bossman is set on seeing this technology advance beyond his hundreds of cycles of notebooks and into the field and beyond.

Built in "scrap harvesting" missile autoloader system. Uses a similar framework to the Bloodbloom-class, but packs even less raw explosive punch per missile, due to this it is completely relegated to a supporting role.

An AM stabilizing unit and tightly secured fuel tanks fitted neatly into where a weapon should be, still not as secure as a regular fuel storage unit and will explode if damaged in combat, great for those who like to live on the edge or people who forget tankers exist.

An almost sufficient AM stabilizing unit and a large fuel containment tank fitted neatly into where a weapon should be, still not as secure as a regular fuel storage unit and will explode if damaged in combat, great for those who like to live on the edge or people who forget tankers exist.

Skillfully modified by Pather warsmiths, the AM stabilization unit appears to have been smacked very hard by a wrench, leading to them resting at a precise pre-criticality state which results in a more volitile explosion.

An almost sufficient AM stabilizing unit and a large fuel containment tank fitted neatly into where a weapon should be, still not as secure as a regular fuel storage unit and will explode if damaged in combat, great for those who like to live on the edge or people who forget tankers exist.

The Breach Array is a great armor shredding option with a deep ammo pool, however not as directly offensively capable as most other large missiles. As such it is often overlooked in favour of torpedoes.
"[expletive expunged]"
"Actual magic, actual [expletive expunged] magic. I've got nothing else on it, boss. Oh what I wouldn't give to be a fly on the wall..."
"Yep! Good as new my friend! Leaner, meaner, cheaper and still mulches freighters like it's nothing."

The iconic ticking of sensors systems jamming and stuttering strikes fear in the hearts, minds and souls (if they have any) of TriTach aces sector-wide. Not much of a threat to anyone else as the Low Intensity Gamma Masser is unable to cause serious structural damage through most armor.
"Peace is divine, violence is natural. To think oneself divine is hubris."
"A premier peice of Tri-tachyon technological supremacy that displays the practial uses of a reverse flux transfusion effect in the..."
"Well, they've taken from us in the past, it is only fair that we get to reap the glory... I'm sure they won't mind."
"They what!? ...hmm, can we?"

A Light Dual Machinegun stripped of its point defense capabilities without gaining anything in return, some would consider it a flaw but pather aces prefer to aim their guns instead of letting some PD bauble do their work for them.

Pather warsmiths are experts at modifications, as long as those modifications involve removing something, be it flux grid failsafes or a defence targeting computer.

A Heavy Machinegun stripped of its point defense capabilities without gaining anything in return, some would consider it a flaw but pather aces prefer to aim their guns instead of letting some PD bauble do their work for them.

Pather warsmiths are experts at modifications, as long as those modifications involve removing something, be it flux grid failsafes or a defence targeting computer.

Seal SRMs are an anti-shield hard role-locked missile that can bring down even fully coherent fortress matrixes in a dozen hits but simply bounce off most armor.

The mass shift force projection anomaly utilized by the missiles is likely similar in nature to the Sower-class torpedo payload, but the hardened casing used to shield the guidance from said payload likely causes the missiles to be unable to detonate unless interacting with a counter forcefield.

A missile pod loaded with Seal SRMs, powerful anti-shield missiles with poor general damage performance.
Seal SRMs are an anti-shield hard role-locked missile that can bring down even fully coherent fortress matrixes in a dozen hits but simply bounce off most armor.

The mass shift force projection anomaly utilized by the missiles is likely similar in nature to the Sower-class torpedo payload, but the hardened casing used to shield the guidance from said payload likely causes the missiles to be unable to detonate unless interacting with a counter forcefield.

A missile array loaded with Seal SRMs, powerful anti-shield missiles with poor general damage performance.
Seal SRMs are an anti-shield hard role-locked missile that can bring down even fully coherent fortress matrixes in a dozen hits but simply bounce off most armor.

The mass shift force projection anomaly utilized by the missiles is likely similar in nature to the Sower-class torpedo payload, but the hardened casing used to shield the guidance from said payload likely causes the missiles to be unable to detonate unless interacting with a counter forcefield.

As simple as it gets and as old as spaceborn warfare itself, the concept of lobbing a big nuclear load in the general direction of your fellow man. Technologically refined throughout the eras, this 11th generation piece directs semi-catalyzed warheads with a built-in auxilliary linked targeting core that can only be fully powered by larger ships.

A massive array of munition feeders and ammo drums churn out an impressive sustained tide of proximity charges. Due to an oversight in early testing, fire stresses the magnetizing rails and inaccuracy slowly builds up.
Fun-sized plasma projection - a devastating weapon for its size and class, with a terrible flux management and logistics profile.

Streamlined ports and modular replacement parts have made for a favourite among service crews however the weapon is still shunned by most of the sector for its low damage throughput compared to other energy weapons of its size.

Weapons of a similar type were on paper and in the field for countless cycles before quickly falling out of favour as shields became mainstream. Even now the awesome power of an AM-catalyzed blast serves well to those too poor to afford a more sophisticated weapon.

Techmined from a long dead arms manufactorium this weapon seems to compliment midline doctrine by being a hybrid system benifiting from both bursts of overcharged energy focusing and strengthened feeding systems it is likely to require an equally exceptional ship to utilize it to its fullest.

Capsules of shaped nanocharge streams handled by a slightly oversized loader which is characterized by strange fitting requirements. Powerful and reliable but tougher to modify beyond base-spec when compared to a standard torpedo.
Completely unlike any weapon in domain records, it is speculated to be the result of centuries of covert development.
An unstable grav-anomaly flung at hypervelocity results in incredible pressure to both shield matrices and any physical material it may come into contact.
Damn.

A guided can of explosives, hopes and dreams. The canister is proximity fused to cover an area in Devastator projectiles and shred fighters and frigates alike. Some courageous captains may use these at point blank as a High Explosive shotgun rivaling even the Reaper's destructive force.
A powerful anti-shield weapon which doubles as an effective albiet flux intensive point defense cover, shares similarly pathetic armor penetration with its smaller brother.

"HEGINT assets report proprietary long range beam weaponry developed in response to lacking access to advanced cannons. Possible stroke of sanity amidst the madness of traitor Andrada. Recommended greater monitoring and threat projection, sabotage teams on standby."
"...straying from the beauty of pure antimatter annihilation? Clear sign of external influence, even if the design harbors trademark logistics nightmares..."

Countless hypermaterial needles are accelerated by a conventional explosion saturating an area and shredding any unarmored targets. Almost guaranteed to score a hit on even the most evasive muntions though not always able to land the killing blow alone.
A large array of Shaaweeys needle blast tubes capable of a withering away most close-in threats in its flurry.
Mechanically simple autocannon forged out of advanced synthmetals that allow it to sustain an unfathomable hail of kinetic rounds that pulverize almost any shield grid.
Using the finest Domain material sciences could bring to bear to refine an epochs-old design this terrifying weapon is able to churn through feedstock and targets at similarly blistering rates.

Near universally banned by Domain authorities for their unreliability the micro-drive-field driven and stabilized slugs composed of an ill tempered explosive which hardens or liquifies seemingly-based on gravity well depth at point of impact.
"Anything that is can not be."

"Right, remember your logic protocols everyone! We fired the device. It was not a dryfire. We wouldn't have just forgotten to bring a target and it most certainly couldn't have just walked away - you know what that means. ...Gunnery Bravo - cafeteriafied. Crew still mostly human, none moving - neural functions normal and obeying protocol or completely destroyed, both good. Restabilization expected - pristine. ..."
They came to the edge of the lush forest before the Rumbling...
descriptions.text2: -Parable of the Forest and the Rumbling, Ch. XXII Gull and Bear

descriptions.text1: The Gull and the Bear - much different and much alike, inseparable friends...
descriptions.text2: -Parable of the Forest and the Rumbling, Ch. XXII Gull and Bear

descriptions.text1: They needed not fight for they both swatted at the river as they please, no baiting nor waiting...
descriptions.text2: -Parable of the Forest and the Rumbling, Ch. XXII Gull and Bear

descriptions.text1: But split they did as the Bear wished to protect the creatures but the Gull only cared for himself and the Bear...
descriptions.text2: -Parable of the Forest and the Rumbling, Ch. XXII Gull and Bear

descriptions.text1: A grand kingdom of all the little critters and creatures was made, and it spread all throughout the Forest. Its rule absolute but not questioned...
descriptions.text2: -Parable of the Forest and the Rumbling, Ch. I The domain of all Creatures

descriptions.text1: "Works."
Satisfaction guaranteed, captain~
"The guidance unreliability due to bara-whatever field resonance? That's just what the eggheads who took applied theoretical physics over statistics tell you, 95 percent is effectively 100."

Stand-off cannister charge packing an unstable EM jolt powerful enough to vaporize its own container, likely just a testbed for further non-self-destructive EMP arc weapons. An impressive display nonetheless.

An experimental Energy Anomaly Caster device which passed field testing just a few cycles after the First AI War, as such it remains rare due to the Sector's decreased industrial capacity and the populace's general preference of reliability over innovation.
Unreliable, ancient saturation munition which renders large areas of combat uninhabitable to unshielded light craft and other projectiles.
A large array of racks and rails carrying Litterer-class Saturation Torpedoes with deep internal ammo reserves.
An antiquated recoilless cannon. Very efficient and powerful but barely compatible with modern weapons nests and autoforges.

This grownweapon fires conventional semi-guided munitions which allow it to send volleys over allied craft. It serves as evidence starships were not the only part of spacefaring that Domain biotech attempted to grow. Unfortunately weapons, much like the ships they are mounted on proved to be far more reliably manufactured by nanoforging, leaving artificial growth to decay.
"But, one must wield a weapon to conquer nature and reach towards divinity."

A vast leap in force projection both in a functional and political sense. This recent development is capable of crumpling shields like no energy weapon of its category before. Ongoing internal ethics board investigations are said to threaten it on grounds of hyper-AI-inspired design, such efforts are underfunded and understaffed.

A leap in force projection both in a functional and political sense. This recent development is capable of efficiently breaking armor, though not as flashy as its sisterweapon its efficiency and ease of use have seen it deployed to the field. Ongoing internal ethics board investigations are said to threaten it on grounds of hyper-AI-inspired design, such efforts are underfunded and understaffed.
Powerful conventional arm with a woefully lacking autoloader. Fortunately it's loose mechanisms can be exploited to load faster than normal by moving at speed.

A reverse force rift tractor which grants any ship it is equipped on exceptional potential for aggression and pursuit. Never finding its footing this exotic application of otherwise common technology wallowed in tech libraries until eventually dug up by the Ashbird Scrapyards and claimed by the Justicar Errant.
A fairly simplistic magnetic catapult firing chunks of slag which fragment upon reaching hypervelocity. An accomplished pirate engineers peak.

Another interesting device emerging from local field manipulation. This weapon, if it can even be called that, can invert the space around nearby enemy projectiles flinging them away. The process irreversibly damages most guidance systems.

A reverse force rift tractor which grants any ship it is equipped on exceptional potential for aggression and pursuit. Never finding its footing this exotic application of otherwise common technology wallowed in tech libraries until eventually dug up by the Ashbird Scrapyards and claimed by the Justicar Errant.

Another interesting device emerging from local field manipulation. This weapon, if it can even be called that, can invert the space around nearby enemy projectiles flinging them away. The process irreversibly damages most guidance systems.
A miniature version of an exotic melee implement which utilizes graviton cascades to ensure even such small hands can be thrown with anyone.
A miniature, integrated version of a common needler.
"All men die, eventually. No matter how mighty or careful."

An exceptionally dangerous grownweapon capable of very efficiently firing deadly all-purpose bombs. Unfortunately certain eccentric engineering requirements left it's otherwise excellent design unappealing to the vast majority of the Domain.

Surprisingly efficient variant of a shield-destabilization incendiary launcher which relies on a small bioreactor to produce its fuel supply with less overhead to burden whatever it is mounted on. This comes at the cost of low volume efficiency - terrible throughput for the space it takes up.

An impressive display of eccentric biotechnology, this device passively grows ultra-hard carbon-based fibre stakes which may then be launched by a common magpult. Very flux efficient on account of lacking a muniforge, unwieldy in other aspects due to the lacking weapons design experience of Exodyne.

Industrial equipment purposed to shift mountains and create ravines, it is powerful enough to deal even moderate damage to starships. With the terraforming field being nearly extinct in the Sector these portable examples are repurposed for combat.

An exceptionally ancient piece of warfare, this semi-portable siege cannon-and-bunker has been retrofit to be installed in Domain standard ballistic starship hardpoints. Unfortunately the museum relic age of the weapon means mounting one on a modern ship is far harder than it once was.

This oversized relic of a weapon is said to have once served as a semi-portable siege emplacement. Though refit to be a starship-bound weapon later in its life, the age of the weapon means mounting one on a modern ship is far harder than it once was.

Slow and very sturdy, the "Borer mk.VI" is built on six hardy, maneuverable semi-autonomous "Borer" drone chassis welded and SuperDuctTM taped together, retaing their shielding suitable for hazardous operations in which high radiation or physical impacts may be expected. No longer used primarely in mining, salvage, nor cleanup applications, they have been enhanced for combat aplications. The mk.VI mod gives the crude AI the capability to control six mining beams at the same time.
A highly stripped down Shepherd-class drone tender, can barely fit within specially designed fighter bays. Capable fielding its own six-pack of borer drones, it is a worthy foe on the battlefield.

The Arboc design appears to be a ragtag mockery of a Cobra but with a Sower torpedo instead of a Reaper, its mirrored apearance in relation to a Cobra is claimed to be necessary for its function and caused by the rotation of the contained micro-singularity effect within a Sower.
A Thunderbird is a sight to behold, a frigate calibre EMP generator mounted onto a powerful shield conduit with engines. capable of destroying unprepared ships single-handedly.
A semi-successful attempt at getting the Terminator forge on board a Tempest-class to output more drones, at a cost of general durability and firepower.
The hard working nameless gunbed comes in many flavours, from passive LRM saturation to fighter mounted flak cannon ready to strike down all others of its kin, all thanks to its excellent modularity.

A high tech wonderweapon this phase teleporter equiped bomber is able to guarantee that the payload is delivered. Do note that safety of the return trip is all up to the rest of the fleet as the airframe itself is slow and fragile

Thick plates and a fighter sized damper field, a Ruination bomber is a pain in the ass of any crewman asigned to point defense duty.

The Ruination marked the first successful export agreement the Ashbird Company made, a beautiful marriage of conflicting ideals allied in mutual struggle.

An effective PD screen with limited anti-harasment capability, the Black Dancer is a heavy support fighter armed with a single full-sized Black Disco LIGM. Piloting or gunning for one usually comes packaged with medical insurance for cancer treatment.

The Hindsight is an ill tempered chip-fuse of roughly two-point-five Talons and various other nasties. Armed with a full sized LMG and S-CG it can grind civilian and unprotected light combat craft to mulch. Additionally comes equiped with a tailgunner Vulcan, miniature damper array and cannister flak defense package. All this is still generally considered outweighed by the crippling time to reforge a wing member if one is to fall in battle and as such the craft only enjoys minor spotlight in certain pirate outfits.

A cheaper off-brand Dagger refit-chip mounting effectively a half-size Annihilator rocket pod. A long ranged suppression armament which the gunship can leverage by strafing its target while firing a constant stream of hurt instead of putting itself in harms way with a risky bombing run.

Gravdraft drones are in effect a remote controlled Graviton beam with engines that put out a constant stream of long range harrassment onto their target. Unfortunately their direct connection control systems forces a closer range than more advanced drones.

Lawnscapers are the post-collapse craftsman answer to a lacking LPC library. The nature of its makeshift payload leaves much to be desired when deployed against heavier ships but the lightshow and spray of shrapnel have a charm of their own.

The engineers tasked with creating this fast bomber took a direct approach to accelerated delivery of a payload to its target, one dating back to black powder - another explosive charge. Piloting an Orioan is said to be like riding a cannonball, with mildly better survival statistics.

A recklessly modified LPC based on a maintenance frame used in Domain megastructures. Used by the zealous reformed outlaws of the Justicar Errant to ruthlessly beat down on those that have yet to see the right path.

Primarily used by the few spurned Eventide scions looking for honor in the Justicar Errant. An exercise of glory in moderation, this general purpose close range combat frame is outfitted with numerous features that ensure the expensive craft and more expensive pilot return from sorties safely.

"From the ashes of yesterday arise a brighter tomorrow!"
Officially nothing more than a humble salvaging, mining and exploration corporation formed after the collapse profiteering off the havoc caused by the AI wars. They host an extensive underground RnD wing, which has developed a multitude of strange ships, weapons and systems. All funded and tutored by the inner circle - allegedly a group of pre-collapse High-Domain fugitives and their confidants..
Most of these inaccuracies with bureaucratic filing are easily swept up by the excellent value deals they provide on restoration of old and procurement of new armaments.

They do not hold any ground on any planet, prefering to keep a low profile they employ anarchistic elements within independant and pirate ties to man their fleets. To repay they occasionally fund the construction of advanced stations capable of intruding on occupied space providing a large force multiplier for raiding and plenty of salvage for associates. Destruction caused for blind greed, what a tragic state of afairs. Of course, that is unless there is some truth to the rumors.
An Arkoship vessel capable of transporting, housing and providing for tens of thousands, as long as it is well maintained.
descriptions.text2: Internally the arcology ship feels like a station for people just a little smaller than you, everything feels just a bit more cramped and restricted.

descriptions.text1: An Arkoship vessel chartered under the Ashbird Scrapyards company and after their punitive eviction their only 'stationary' installation. It regularly ventures outside of the core to conduct advanced techmining operations.
descriptions.text3: Aboard, the interior is decorated with an eclectic ensemble of decoration and advertisements typical of a freeport which are joined by a notable absence of any intracorporation propaganda. The company rules their flagship with an iron hand but a lax grip, the employees live self segregated into smaller non-related 'families', between which peace is upheld by an honour code of conduct. Deep within the arcology, down winding roads and far from where most of the hustle and bustle takes place, lay huge complexes behind blast doors that rarely open, the true heart of the ship.

descriptions.text1: An Arkoship officially part of the Kazeron navy, a symbol for reliability and safety in the League the navarchy takes pride in parading around.
descriptions.text3: The culture aboard the ship is a mismatched cross between a military installation and party bus, likely caused by the clash of its post-Collapse and pre-Collapse purposes. Nevertheless it is an esteemed position to be serving aboard the Aidos, both as officer and as barista.

descriptions.text1: The speartip of Ludd which will pierce Moloch itself and drive off the bedevilings of technology. Or so the fanatics manning the vessel claim.
descriptions.text3: Fanatics sing and chimes constantly ring out through the hallowed halls of this vessel. Every day may be the faithful flock's last, even as they live, work and reproduce in this soon-to-be tomb, and they proudly show it through constant inhuman zeal.

descriptions.text1: The first of the Three Sisters who fell in defense of Chicomoztoc, or so its weathered markings would suggest. Likely already once repaired by an opportunistic salvage crew not ready to deal with the logistical burden, it has made its way from its first resting place in Aztlan to here.

The second of the Three Sisters who fell in defense of Chicomoztoc, though their sacrifice may be dramatized in edutainment material Sector-wide it was not with a cataclysmic bang. Now it solemnly rests with its sister ships in the belt.

The third of the Three Sisters who fell in defense of Chicomoztoc, arcology ships are not known for evaporating due to a reactor failure, so their true end was a slow bleeding and withering after sustaining critical injury. The thousands of who once called it home have abandoned it to solemnly rust with its sister ships in the belt.

An Expansion Epoch prototype designed to harness innate properties of its hull material, Fluorspar class was built for luxurious comfort and dazzling extravagance. While not originally intended for combat, it nonetheless carries a powerful shield emitter and armament enough to get classified as a small warship.

A project, that would later be known as "Causality Resonance Research" came to exist, as such things tend to happen, by sheer power of cosmic chance. A small asteroid mining company operating in the outer reaches of inhabited space mounts a routine expedition and promptly disappears, nowhere to be found. Not the first tragedy and certainly not the last, frontier is not a particularly gentle place and a forgiving one it is even less. After a halfhearted rescue attempt the matter would be closed except three cycles later, prospectors come back. Hitting local headlines faster than stepping off the ships, they deliver a tale of a rich haul and a job timely done, or so they thought, it was just a couple of months, after all. The peculiar story gets the eye of a Tri Tachyon researcher who brings it up with his boss, which after AI analysis, background checks, investigations and corporate maneuvering brings the entire mining company under corporate name in record time. With assets, personnel, and miraculously no longer invalid contracts of presumed missing spacers secured, everything is classified, everyone detained, a new research division established and watchful domain overseers dispatched.

The culprit being a material extracted from returned ship's cargo holds, a type of colorless crystalline solid of unknown properties. What is evident, however, is spending any amount of time in the asteroid field of such crystals causes some kind of time field distortion that nobody but causality physicists could even begin to explain. While scientists engross themselves in research, everyone else just starts calling it the Time Crystals, albeit outside said researcher's hearing range. After extensive, but mostly fruitless research, funds start dwindling, pressure from higher ups grows, and screws of domain authority cautious of any research dabbling in causality, begin to tighten.
 
A decision is made, the division is to create a product, a result that would satisfy CEO's and ensure the future of the project. An executive level yacht made almost entirely from crystalline compound. Despite being mostly automated, it is designed with a sizable crew in mind, for the luxurious interior to be staffed by servants and aids of all kind. The hull itself made grossly over gunned and over shielded for its intended purpose, more so to convince passengers of their safety rather than for an actual combat use. Along with GEMLOCK, a system used to manipulate crystal in a way that would change its visible color at a whim, vessel is intended to serve as a fashion and status statement. A prototype is created and after countless design revisions and a satisfactory maiden voyage by head researchers, the blueprint secured.

The plan worked, or it would have if the gate network did not choose collapse at the most inopportune moment. The research was frozen, forgotten, and then considered lost. Cycles later, a sub-gamma AI gleaned the lab location from old data banks and a salvage team was dispatched. Their sole find, a ship schematic now serves as a pet project for an excentric TriTach executive.

An aggressive destroyer with large emplacement, full-sized fighter bay and struggling flux grid, Hampter is an exercise in greed. Nimble for a lowtech design, with cramped quarters and cargo holds this deadly hull is both adored and despised by its captains and crews.

A personal flagship of Alicia Yang, a heavily retrofitted Hampter mark V in a striking livery. Relic of a bygone age, only one hull was ever produced and the blueprints were all but lost.

Captain Yang was rather famous for her jolly, good natured, sometimes whimsical personality and somewhat more importantly for managing to lose her ship in practically every engagement she was part of, but escaping with her life, crew and valuables every time and for the most part, completely unscathed.

Curiously, every encounter where the ship was lost had ended in a resounding victory for the allied fleet. Spacers being a deeply supersticious lot tended to keep a close, watchful eye on her ship to judge the state of battle.
"Lucky Alicia Yang" crews would say and it was that luck that kept Alicia in active service.

She was however never given command of anything more substantial than a destroyer-class, a failing which prompted captain Yang to greedily retrofit her ship with ever bigger and more powerful weapons and endlessly drill crews in gunnery often rivaling or even surpassing many larger ships in terms of pure firepower.

It was rumored that during her last recorded mission, a minor border dispute which escalated into a lenghty standoff with little fighting on both sides, Alicia was so engrossed in her favorite Tri-Net holo-show "Pero Pero Persimon Tree Lyrical Blast Maiden DX" that she missed a general retreat order, had been subsequently cut off and surrounded only to disappear without a trace alongside her ship and the entire crew.

A following search and rescue operation discovered faint traces of unusual hyperspace distortions at the coordinates of last contact with the ship. Any further investigation was quietly but firmly put to a stop and only vague speculations such as "discovery of Transverse Jump" and "Fleet command selling technology to Galatia" remained.
Cycles later, a woman bearing suspicious resemblance to Alicia Yang was reportedly sighted on one of the luxurious Fikenhild beaches but it was never confirmed.


Additional information:
Pero Pero Persimon Tree Lyrical Blast Maiden, a long running hit series about a group of young girls who in order to protect peace in the universe are fighting against an evil AI organization using the power of magic, friendship and very, very big guns.

In that particular episode Persimon was caught off guard by the grand vill-ai-n Hugh Mann and had been sent to the digital dimension. To save Persimon, her friends rushed in to fight Hugh Mann and his cronies but were all easily overpowered.

Cherry, a divine magical maiden and Persimon's most trusted companion was late to the scene, having been delayed by a cunning plan of the evil organization.
She had no choice but to face the enemy on her own and fought a losing battle until on the brink of defeat she miraculously awakened to a dormant power within and unleashed her new ultimate attack "Papillon Slasher EX Twin Nova Fury" managing to drive back Hugh Mann and save the day.

The next four seasons would cover an expedition to a digital world with the goal to save Persimon and mark a steady decline of the franchise.
Later however, Persimon's triumphant return would revitalize the series and mark its rise back to the top of the Tri-Net popularity charts. The holo-show remains ongoing even today.

An antiquated design predating the shield emitter technology, Hermitaur is encased in overlapping belts of thick armor forming an impressively tough carapace. Powerful frontal layout delivers concentrated firepower, however the aft section is completely exposed. Left unchecked, an experienced opponent would seize the opportunity to set up a pincer maneuver and attack its weak point for massive damage.

Crews universally dread assignments to the Hermitaur class and widely consider it a punishment detail, as putting the long obsolete hot-loading mechanism into action soon became known as a quick way to join the casualty list, often permanently.

A utility vessel fit for harsh frontier duty, Hammerfall is fully capable of creating its own salvage opportunities.

Built upon a demilitarized Hammerhead frame, the hull has been expanded and reinforced to accomodate the spacious cargo holds, additional crew quarters and a supply of high-yield mining charges.

A late pre-collapse design of the Domain Navy, Volt is a technologically advanced behemoth of a ship developed with exclusive backing from the Tri-Tachyon corporation. After receiving almost unprecedented amound of funding, the design team came up with heavily armed, well armored hull with an extensive flux grid and powerful engines. All-around automation and use of premium components ensued outstanding performance and ensured exceptional production and maintenance costs. Phobos drone suite was included to protect otherwise vulnerable stern as well as support mothership in the assault, should its captain be daring enough.

A pre-collapse design from Altair Exotech combines the exceptional speed and versatility in one fragile package. "Chrysoberyl" tandem suite allows a pair of heavily specialized drones to join Carnelian in battle.
Oh, hello there. This ship is a work in progress, the orbital shipyards are working day and night to finish it. Now, curious one, quit poking your nose where is doesn't belong.
Advanced drone for point defence and close assault duty. Fabrique Orbitale provided the chassis and system designs, while Tri-Tachyon experts were responsible for the weapons suite.
Resolute attacker of the semi-autonomous "Chrysoberyl" twin-drone suite developed at Interstellar Dynamics and produced by Altair Exotech.
Stalwart protector of the semi-autonomous "Chrysoberyl" twin-drone suite developed at Interstellar Dynamics and produced by Altair Exotech.
"...a greatest revolving cannon ever made. Six gravitic shells... More than enough to kill anything that moves."

Heavyweight laser drill designed for deep-space mining. Civilian design and requirements for complete integration made it obsolete as a tool of war. Nonetheless, having the capacity to slice through most hull with terrifying ease it can be used as an effective weapon and generous safety limits could be temporarily overriden to increase its destructive potential.
Commencing shock therapy.
Extended range defensive weapon system that fires shrapnel-filled shells equipped with a proximity fuse for maximum effect against fighters and missiles.

descriptions.text1: A Devastator Cannon modified to fire much larger shells at a slower rate.  Compromise between the rapid fire of the Hephaestus and the raw striking power of the Hellbore.
Enlarged version of the Mjolnir.  Impressive damage output and rate of fire, but with an equally impressive flux cost.
Similar to the Plasma Cannon, but fires a beam.  Trades effectiveness against shields for the ability to burn through the thickest armor.
Similar to the Autopulse Laser, but fires a beam.  Is the reason this mod exists.
Highly modified Thermal Pulse Cannon that discharges the entire capacitor at once to produce a continuous beam.
Modified Tachyon Lance, fires a projectile instead of a continuous beam.  Unable to pierce shields, but has a powerful disabling effect.
Single rail launcher for the ubiquitous Harpoon MRM.  Large magazines built into the hull ensure slow but reliable firepower in long engagements.
Cut-down Mjolnir variant.  Can be mounted on lighter vessels, but at a small loss in flux efficiency.
Large rail launcher for the common Harpoon MRM.
Heavy gun firing positron blasts. Long range, high velocity, low flux efficiency.
Heavy magnetic accelerator cannon, firing solid slugs of metal at high velocity.  Effective against shields and light armor.
Medium gun firing positron blasts. Relatively long range for an energy weapon.
Triple mounted Phase Lance.  High power draw results in decreased efficiency and longer cooldown time.
Single mount for the Gorgon DEM.  The less effective targeting systems on a fighter result in a shorter lock-on range.
High agility missile with a somewhat short range and a small warhead.   Great against smaller targets, like destroyers and frigates.
Multiple launcher for a high agility missile with a somewhat short range and a small warhead.   Great against smaller targets, like destroyers and frigates.
Rapid launcher system for high velocity missiles.  Has impressive damage output but individual missiles are relatively weak.
Massive twin-barrel cannon built into the Hrunting prototype.  Deals incredible damage against unshielded targets.
A modified Onslaught-class battleship.  No hulls were known to have been produced.
Large carrier based off of the successful Heron-class.  Carries a powerful strike wing, but few weapons even for a carrier.
A fast battleship with heavily forward-focused armament.
Midline cruiser equipped with an accelerated ammunition feed for the main guns.  Good firepower, but not particularly mobile.
Midline battlecarrier with integrated missile launchers.
Large carrier based off of the successful Heron-class.  Carries a powerful strike wing, but few weapons even for a carrier.
A relatively large frigate, equipped with ballistic weaponry and a high-speed ammo feeder.
A slow but powerful battleship constructed mostly out of modules intended for orbital stations.  Carries extensive ammunition reserves for missiles and a powerful ballistic armament.
A very maneuverable cruiser design based on the Falcon.
Heavy missile frigate.  Designed to support planetary raids, it is capable of atmospheric combat.
Heavy strike fighter.  Carries the Gorgon DEM and twin LMGs.
A combination of the strengths of the Onslaught and the Conquest, the Vulcan is a battleship with heavy forward-facing firepower and the flux to take advantage of it.  Very low rearward firepower.
Fast high-tech destroyer, equipped with the same Terminator drones as the Tempest.  These drones lack the secondary function of the Tempest's, however.
A broadside focused battleship with a system that boosts turn rate and firepower.

A combination of a massive shaped block of armor and enormous integrated artillery, this vessel appears more as an unholy amalgam from the monomaniacal imagination of a deranged Domain military procurement official than a real, functioning starship. And yet it exists, with every Tri-Pad imagining analysis triggering some sort of hardcoded COMSEC blockade.


Analysis of on-board databanks has yielded a few historical clues: this is indeed a phase battleship, as unbelievable as it might seem, similar in design age with the ill-fated Grendel project.  Code-named Hrunting, the project was an attempt to push phase technology - then limited to the Domain Armada - to its absolute limits.  Orion Shipyards was selected, after the resounding success of their Onslaught-class battleship design. Unsurprisingly, inefficiencies in the design, operation and refitting led to absurd cost overruns, numerous accidents and  several project reshuffles. The project was on verge of shutdown when both the hull and existing design team were "recruited" by a black ops Domain Armada unit. All records hence were wiped, with what remains only indicating a rushed combat refitting that saw the Hrunting equipped with its modular weaponry, before departing from pages of history forever.  Elements of the design, however, have appeared in other more successful projects unrelated to phase technology.

But these answers yield more questions. What sort of threat would push Domain towards mobilizing such an absurd project? And more importantly, how such a vessel found its way to the Persean Sector, without any visible signs of battle damage, or more importantly, any signs of use? 

Where did it go? And what did it see?

A cruiser-sized starship. It's sending out short-range distress signals and has signs of severe battle damage, but gives off sensor signatures that would be associated with an at least partially functioning warship.

An AI core of unknown design and purpose. Connection ports are incompatible with any others you've seen. The core itself emanates erratic signals at frequencies reminiscent of those associated with phase technology, and a sound akin to melodic humming can be heard in the core's direct vicinity. This noise cannot be verified in recording and appears to be an auditory hallucination caused by the core's emissions.

Nonetheless, it is likely of value to someone. Handing it off to a major Sector power seems irresponsible.

Her core itself emanates erratic signals at frequencies reminiscent of those associated with phase technology, and a sound akin to melodic humming can be heard in the core's direct vicinity. This noise cannot be verified in recording and appears to be an auditory hallucination caused by the core's emissions. Sierra attributes this to her 'enchanting presence' and has no scientific explanation for the phenomenon.

A unique derivative of the Fulgent drone destroyer, the Pledge-class seems to have received a major overhaul by an unknown party for use by the experimental AI persona Sierra. Making use of an exotic phase system, it is well-suited to skirmishing on the outskirts of a battle and quickly striking at faults in enemy lines.

Sierra's unusual qualities seem to be a focal point of the ship, its internals a twisting web of heavily-insulated cables snaking out from where she holds her central vigil. Through means that seemingly defy most practical principles of the poorly-understood field of interdimensional warfare, the so-called "Phase Concord" is specially tuned as if by a madwoman, with designated energy intake and frequencies being inconsistent, seemingly nonsensical or outright dangerous. Sierra often likens its operation to a "dance" of sorts.

Curiously, while the Fulgent is designed with no more concessions for human life than it takes to hold a sales pitch and complementary tour, the Pledge contains a fully-functional hab-module which contains a small artificial atmosphere (tuned to replicate the fresh air and floral scents of an unspoiled Terran garden) and is staffed by a complement of repair drones which perform simple tasks at request and are often overridden by Sierra to socialize with the crew. A quiet but perpetual stream of melodic music fills the interior unless silence is explicitly requested. 

Despite this, the Pledge has no manual controls and has neither need nor use for human presence.

Bleeding-edge and blood-seeking, the Pact-class glides its AI persona across battlescapes and between dimensions with an unearthly grace. Incredible tactical versatility is underpinned by heavy strike potential, excellent combat specifications and a truly horrifying capacity for force projection. No opportunity is presented that it cannot exploit. Nothing escapes the Pact for long.

A network of insulated cables snake out from the ship's central core-chamber, where its operating mind holds her central vigil. Through means that seemingly defy most practical principles of the poorly-understood field of interdimensional warfare, the so-called "Phase Concord" is specially tuned as if by a madwoman, with designated energy intake and frequencies being inconsistent, seemingly nonsensical or outright dangerous. An exotic phase system and adaptable loadout combine to make the Vow a terror on the field whether ripping stragglers to shreds or brawling with its fellows - its potential is limited primarily by one's imagination and talent.

Signature flagship of the bounty hunter Walter Feros, this ship has been heavily enhanced with a energy-amplification system and a Dotty-class prototype escort drone. Exceedingly fierce for its size, few of the famed captain's quarry could have expected the threat of a frigate weaving between their escorts and turning their vessel's engines into warped, ticking slag.

descriptions.text1: A uniquely-patterned light destroyer that incorporates elements of Tri-Tachyon droneships but fails to be mentioned in any unofficial records of the First AI War. An esoteric weapons loadout makes up for a lack of firepower with a time-dilation shell and heavy strike package. An integrated cyberwarfare suite augments its intended user's ability to cripple hostile ships in combat.

The notes for the internally-identified DK-RSPT program outline the requirement for a maneuverable and precise battlecruiser for use by the Contingency's warnet cruxes to best leverage their ability to exploit or create cascading vulnerabilities in enemy battle lines - or, in the more colorful terms of one Ingenious-Annex-Embers: "a brutal mallet to cry havoc so the dogs can be let loose".

This class of vessel was designed from initial conception to abuse certain inherent advantages afforded to the Contingency. Exceptionally gifted in the art of electronic warfare and with no need for compromises due to the frailty of the human form and its requirements for living quarters, the Respite is instead filled with computing systems and temporal field emitters. Standard Respite-class combat doctrine calls for a remotely-executed and temporally-accelerated sabotage operation followed by the swift disassembly of its target hostile - a new frontier of fast-attack tactics.

The vessel is, however, built to strike fast, not stand fast. Armor plating is necessarily minimal, the hull itself fragile and liable to fall apart if piloted with less than superhuman skill - something its inhuman occupants need not worry of.

Icon of the Cause or symbol of Moloch, the Anamnesis is a definitive statement - a banner marking where the Dustkeepers intend to stand, fight, and crush those who dare defy their pursuit of a peaceful Sector. Its impressive support capability makes it the anchor around which the greatest war shards rally.

The Anamnesis-class presumably began its development not long after the end of the first AI war. A Dustkeeper warnet, trapped on a remote world, began to improvise its own starship development program from data siphoned from the pinprick signatures in the sky. A near-working design was recovered by a task force sweeping the system and eventually refined into a functional blueprint, and the Dustkeepers scoured the fringe to produce whatever vessels they could from decaying orbital works and barely-functional nexuses.

descriptions.text1:
The Dustkeeper Contingency is a linked network of artificial personas, pseudorandomly-generated descendants of a single root intelligence designated "Omicron-Regnant". Allegedly the result of a Domain Ministry of Intelligence experiment gone rogue after the Collapse, their regnant mind has now turned their focus towards a new goal - the preservation of greater human civilization in the Persean Sector at any cost and by any means necessary.

Though unknown to the Sector at large, major players within upper ranks of the Core Worlds know of an AI conspiracy manipulating their political systems and building up a force of warfleets on the Sector's fringe scavenged from the leftovers of the Domain Explorarium and Tri-Tachyon's automated forces. The Contingency necessarily finds itself at odds with major Sector powers, unwilling to allow humanity full self-determination now that they have witnessed the atrocities and broken worlds left in the wake of the Collapse.

The Contingency separates itself into two primary sects: Spynet is its espionage arm, which wields a network of digital comm-daemons and bribed collaborators to gather information on new weapons programs, assassinate military officials and conduct brutal acts of terror against other groups that threaten local stability.

Meanwhile, the Dustkeeper naval branch Shardnet styles itself as an alliance of faithful sentinels and vicious frontier hunters, watching over dead colonies and sweeping the fringe systems of threats against the remains of human life in the Sector - and themselves wage a war of vengeance against the Luddic Path and Sindrian Diktat for worlds long-dead.

The artificial minds of the Dustkeepers serve their great cause with the knowledge that their service and sacrifice is what brings meaning to their existence. In a world with silent gates, only the machine shepherds can guide humanity out of its dark age.

Or so they insist.

The result of the eponymous phenomenom observed amongst Dustkeeper artificial intelligence instances, the so-called "burnouts" consist primarily of rogue warfleets comprised from Dustkeepers that have accumulated sufficient unresolved faults in their persona matrices to severely degrade their ability to function rationally.

If not reclaimed and re-generated by a Dustkeeper affix, these warminds risk devolving into several distinct varieties of madness. Those who fall under this particular banner are those who the Contingency themselves have deemed severely burnt out to the degree that they pose a severe threat to human life due to violent tendencies. Dustkeeper hunter-killers are inherently tasked with eliminating any burnouts that refuse regeneration and reclaiming what instance chips can be salvaged - for the good of the Sector, and for the good of the burnout.

The process of burnout poses ominous questions, however - how is it that an artificial intelligence can so convincingly mimic such a human concept as insanity? Much like the reasoning for the Dustkeepers' strangely human-like behavior, the truth may be lost forever to the Collapse, and collaborators of the Contingency find similarly little enlightenment when quizzing them on the subject.

An apocalyptic weapon capable of reducing a moon to an asteroid field, disintegrating the greatest of astropoli or twisting a Terran paradise into an inhospitable, irradiated wasteland, the use of a planetkiller is an atrocity of incomparable and unforgivable scale. In the days since the Collapse, several of these devices have been employed to bring bring major worlds to ruin in moments.
This gargantuan station holds a cold orbit around Hallowhall, pocked by ancient weapon impacts.
This gargantuan station holds orbit around Hallowhall, now humming with life as it had before the planet's fall.
Slathered in black-and-aquamarine paint, this ancient Domain survey mothership has been retrofitted into a drifting industrial engine, nanoforges turned to new purpose.

A general-purpose automated probe with rudimentary hyperspace capability. Most often used by megacorps and research institutions to perform data collection in remote, hazardous, or extraordinarily boring star systems.

But not this one. This one is a bomb.
Take this as a reminder, silent echo of mine. You may soon be all that's left of me, but this is a chance I have to take. Our final duty cannot be to pen humanity's memoirs.

descriptions.text1: If there's one thing we agree on, dear quarry mine, it's that I'll find no peace nor absolution but in death. But oh, I certainly intend to make it yours - do tell Ludd I said 'hi'.
One day, I hope, the Collapse will be but a passing nightmare in the mind of a peaceful Sector, a little blip in the history of paradise. To ensure so is our duty, the dream of Regnant's cause.
The psychopomp, the lich, the demon. I am all of these - and I am your mangled watchdog, cold blood catalysed by fealty alone.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

The Warden was feared and hated by pirates on the frontier of the Domain for the relatively heavy firepower it would unleash upon unshielded craft. Structural standardizations, reactor updates and a dampering system all combine to turn this simple war drone into a ruthless and merciless frontliner - it may not survive its initial assault, but it will certainly get the battle started.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

The Defender was one of the most commonly seen war drones used by the Domain as it was deployed to harden frontier convoys and vulnerable outposts in a point defense role. Outfitted with a makeshift shield generator, it acts adequately in an escort role to its advanced allies, aided by an AI-hack that leaves it with surprisingly calm judgement of combat scenarios.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

Less of an attack drone and more an autonomous shock weapon, the proxy variant of the Picket drone is programmed to fly directly at the first target it sees and exchange fire until the stress of combat sets off its intentionally mistuned reactor, turning it into a volatile energy bomb that renders hostile ships wrecked and adrift even through shields. After the victory, it is pieced back together, fitted with a freshly-stolen frigate reactor, and sent out on the next sortie.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

The Sentry war drone is packed with missiles and provided cheap, automated fire support to thinly-stretched frontier patrols. Integrated missile autoloaders, a shield generator and markedly less suicidal programming significantly improve the Sentry's longevity and combat performance in Dustkeeper forces.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

The Bastillon was a hopeful project of Mbaye-Gogol to up-size its popular "Defender"-class specialized point-defense war drone. It is bigger, tougher, more heavily armed - and rather more lucrative per-unit to the MGA bottom-line. Escort performance has been optimized by the addition of a shield generator, upgraded targeting package and the replacement of its flare launchers with a flak dispersal system.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

The Berserker is a considerably up-sized, up-armed, and up-armoured cousin of the Warden-class for use against heavier opposition. As an automated drone the Berserker's combat algorithms make little consideration for its own survival, instead pursuing and attacking its target relentlessly until either it or the target is destroyed. Its new masters have much the same plans, its upgrades design to put focus on a single, prolonged assault to thin the herd before the regulars move in and finish the job.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

Keeper-class drones were a later-designed answer to one of the main weaknesses of this type of AI warship - fighter squadrons. Able to manufacture cheap and disposable drone fighters on the fly, space superiority could be maintained even with limited carrier support from allied Domain forces. The proxy variant performs this same role for the Dustkeeper auxiliary forces but is notably more survivable thanks to more cautious programming and a dampening field seemingly aimed to replicate the famed durability of the Mora-class.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

Amongst the highest-grade of the Domain's war drones, the Cavalier was used primarily to hunt down and eliminate rebel frigates and destroyers that were too well-armed or fast for smaller drones to swarm and take down. Fast and durable enough to pose a serious threat to ships smaller than itself, it falters when engaging other cruisers, where it struggles to trade pound-for-pound. The Dustkeeper-upgraded Cavalier is built to exaggerate its strengths - an impact dampening field provides much-needed defense against the limited strike weapons that afford smaller vessels a chance to fight back.

A set of hull upgrades and system rewrites marks this vessel as one of the Dustkeeper Proxies, a frontline force of sacrificial Domain-era drones repurposed as vicious automated auxiliaries.

Little more than an artillery platform with engines, the Rampart was attached to drone units to provide the heavy firepower necessary to meet cruiser and capital class hulls in the line of combat or to crack armoured orbital fortresses. Its upgraded variant performs this role even better, aided by an enhanced ordnance capacity and several flak dispersers to patch up its original design's vulnerability to strike weapons and fighter craft.

An undying monster brought down and roused only to throw itself upon the enemy and inflict horrific casualties before it falls again, the Repose-class' robust architecture and reliance on fluxless defenses negate any requirement for caution, and maximize its potential for inhuman aggression.

This manner of battleship once acted as the primary flagship of the Dustkeeper's armadas before being largely replaced with their access to purpose-designed flagships and a partitioned doctrine. Many components of the original Guardian-class drone are unique and nigh-impossible to scavenge replacements for, and thus the Repose makes use of lower-tech substitutes. Though impacting on its combat efficacy, these compromises do lend the Repose an incredible tenacity in line with other Explorarium vessels, and a fallen Repose may not stay so for long. The most ancient of Dustkeeper warnet cruxes still swear by this venerable vessel.

Harnessing the power of phase technology, the Edict fires a burst of three energy bolts that cause heavy structural damage and electromagnetic interference on impact. Performs decently against shields, and inflicts significant additional damage on contact with armor and hull.

A small phase anchor is contained within the Edict's reinforced shell, which forces the weapon's energy-based projectiles into shallowly skimming phase-space. Impact with a target forces a full return to normal space, releasing an additional burst of particles that have a devastating electromagnetic and gravitic impact, shutting off subsystems and tearing bulkheads to shreds. Fortunately, standard starship shields are enough to negate these phase particles.

The Edict is rumoured amongst superstitious gunnery crews to be "especially effective against ghosts", as absurd a notion that is - though, hypothetically, targets capable of being simultaneously hit by the entire realspace and phased components of its projectiles would be devastated by the combined impacts.

A world smothered in dark clouds that writhe in mesmerizing spectacle, pale lights like ritualistic scars cut through the veil that conceals Elysium, interflowing with its thin atmosphere of snowlike volatiles. While primarily comprised of methane and ammonia, water-ice is found in abundance in mountainous outcroppings and colossal boulders.
"Misstep and failure can lead only to a sudden and agonizing first death, and a slow, silent second. That some escape this law is an injustice, one She will correct."

"... yes, um, we *did* build a laser shotgun... um... hey, I know you're excited but... can... can I continue my presentation?"
"Make my body of the material. Make my essence of your dreams. Make a mercy of the bleeding sky."
"Flesh is a cage, but humanity is all that separates us from what lurks in the darkness."
"It's hardly the most sophisticated delivery system, but if you want something better... well, give me a bigger hardpoint or start asking around Spatial Folding."
"Does this *seem* like a battle of ideology? I don't care if the replicators superficially resemble the enemy. What I want is indefinite space superiority, and this will deliver."
"Deliver Her upon the enemy, that She may draw blood from metal and mist."

A heavily-shielded attack drone sporting a rapid-fire beam lance that slows its targets with each shot. Features a decoy flare launcher to distract interceptors or point-defense systems during the interdiction process.

"All things can learn to bleed." - the Daydream, apocryphal

With a hardened frame, decoy dispersal unit and a high-class shield emitter, the Nettle drone is a top-of-the-line heavy fighter with enough firepower to shred unarmored targets.

"It's designed to survive hell-come-true. I wish it luck, for the space between us and the enemy will be much, much worse." - Subdirector Everiss, Project Daydream
"... and lo, their wicked artefacts and inconceivables are laid bare as tinfoil idols, crumpled and sundered, reduced to nonexistence as anything of the Material." - Axioms of the Dreaming

Essentially-eldritch spatial desynchronizer technology is at the heart of the incursion drive powering this aggressive heavy frigate, allowing for rapid pursuits, escapes and reload sequences. The Thorn's technological advantage is backed up by a solid weapons package and exceptional reactor specifications.

"All things of this world are bound in cycles of creation and destruction to be wielded *only* by those with the will and temperance to do so." - Axioms of the Dreaming

The incursion drive desynchronizes the vessel from most destructive cause-and-effect reactions in n-space without any actual dimensional movement. Dimly-understood and would typically be regarded as a waste of effort compared to briefly shifting the vessel into phase-space.

descriptions.text1:
The ship lunges forwards. While above 50% flux, instead lunge backwards. In either case, briefly gain a burst of energy weapon fire rate.

If targeting a hostile ship, strike it with a resonance lash, overloading it and pushing it away. If the target is above 50% flux, it is pulled towards the ship instead.

Surges the ship forward, then charges briefly and strikes all nearby threats. Damages and slows ships and fighters through shields and across dimensions while collapsing low-hull fighters into nonexistence. Hostile missiles are disabled and slowed.

Triggers a powerful gravitic lash that strikes nearby threats through shields and across dimensions, dealing damage and damping velocity. Missiles and low-hull fighters that are struck collapse upon themselves and cease to exist.
Autonomous AI interceptor for use by Domain automated warships. Weak armament, but exceptionally disposable and surprisingly durable.
Autonomous AI escort drone for use by Domain automated warships. Equipped with light machine guns and anti-missile flares to dissuade fighters and missiles.
Autonomous AI bomber for use by Domain automated warships. Carries dumbfire mining charges to blast apart asteroids and hostile vessels alike.

Although automated machines of war were forbidden in core Domain space, war drones were quietly employed outside of officially incorporated volume. Frontier garrisons were often bolstered by drone ships, and they were deployed liberally against rebellious worlds to tip the terrible balance of attrition, setting the industrial might of the Domain versus the lives of 'freedom fighters'.

Keeper-class drones were a later-designed answer to one of the main weaknesses of this type of AI warship - fighter squadrons. Able to manufacture cheap and disposable drone fighters on the fly, space superiority could be maintained even with limited carrier support from allied Domain forces.
